114|---
115|
116|## 3. Where the logs live
117|
118|There are **four** distinct log sources. Match the question to the source.
119|
120|### 3a. Service / request logs — container logs or systemd journal
121|
122|The production API logs Fastify structured JSON (`level`, `time`, `pid`,
123|`req`, `res`, `msg`). Where to read it depends on the deployment shape:
124|
125|```bash
126|# Docker Compose deployment
127|docker compose logs -f backend     # tail live service logs
128|docker compose logs --tail 200 backend
129|docker compose ps                  # confirm the service is up
130|
131|# Native self-host (systemd user unit)
132|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -f
133|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -n 200
134|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> --since "2026-10-29 08:00:00"
135|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 100
136|systemctl --user status <service-unit>
137|systemctl --user restart <service-unit>
138|```
139|
140|Use this for: request failures, startup crashes, unhandled errors, and
141|confirming the service is up. On a native self-host the unit file is
142|typically at `~/.config/systemd/user/<service-unit>` (WorkingDirectory
143|`{{deployDir}}/api`, `PORT` set to the API port, `NODE_ENV=production`).
144|
145|### 3b. Deploy logs — `<deploy-state-dir>/`
146|
147|Self-deployment state and logs live under the deploy state directory
148|(typically `~/.kainbain/deploy/` when self-hosting KainBain):
149|
150|```text
151|<deploy-state-dir>/
152|├── deploy.log        # full deploy script output (append-only)
153|├── state.json        # current deploy state
154|├── last-result.json  # last deploy result
155|├── history.jsonl     # append-only deploy history (one JSON per line)
156|├── build.txt         # autoincrementing build counter
157|├── deploy.lock       # flock lock file
158|└── releases/         # per-build release snapshots
159|```
160|
161|The live build number is stamped into `{{deployDir}}/build.json`
162|(`{ buildNumber, deployedAt, commit }`). The header shows `#B<number>` — clicking
163|it opens the KainBain changelog baked into the deploy (`{{deployDir}}/changelog.json`,
164|latest 200 commits on the default branch plus `totalCount`). On Docker
165|deployments the build files live inside the image, not on the host — use the
166|API (`GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/changelog`) instead of host paths.
167|
168|```bash
169|tail -n 200 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
170|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
171|cat <deploy-state-dir>/state.json
172|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
173|```
174|
175|Use this for: "did the deploy succeed / what build is live / why did it roll
176|back". The API also exposes these via `GET /deploy/status`, `GET /deploy/log`,
177|`POST /deploy`, `POST /deploy/rollback`, plus `GET /deploy/changelog` for the
178|baked history (`{ changelog: null, reason: "not-baked" }` before the first
179|deploy that bakes it).
180|
181|### 3c. Agent session transcripts — worktree (Runner) or `.kainbain/sessions/` (embedded)
182|
183|Runner-executed stages keep their session where the harness ran: the
184|per-task worktree on the **Runner host** (`sessionDir` = the worktree), not on
185|the backend. Only embedded (non-Runner) runs write transcripts to the
186|backend's `<project cwd>/.kainbain/sessions/` — one JSONL transcript per
187|session (one JSON object per line): `session`, `model_change`,
188|`thinking_level_change`, and message/tool events, resumed via the SDK's
189|`SessionManager`.
190|
191|```bash
192|ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/
193|head -5 {{projectCwd}}/.kainbain/sessions/*.jsonl
194|```
195|
196|Use this for: the raw agent conversation / model used / thinking level for a
197|project. Always check **which host ran the stage** first — for Runner tasks
198|the transcript is on the Runner host, and the backend directory may not have
199|it. Note: `.kainbain/` is gitignored, so these are local-only.
200|
201|### 3d. Per-task logs — `# Log Entries` in `task.md`, Live Console on the wire
202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a
206|running task, watch the socket (see §4b), not the file. `task.md` is
207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and
208|`# Log Entries` stay current, but there is no rendered process-log tail to
209|`tail -f` anymore.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 4. Analysing a **live** task
214|
215|A "live" task is one currently executing or queued. The engine is a single
216|global executor (`ExecutionQueue`) with an `engineState` snapshot.
217|
218|### 4a. Via the API (fastest, no filesystem)
219|
220|```bash
221|# Engine state: what is running right now
222|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
223|
224|# Full observability: engine + health + build + task metrics
225|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
226|
227|# Health
228|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
229|
230|# List tasks for a project (projectId optional → active project)
231|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
232|
233|# Single task (full state incl. history, reports, log entries)
234|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/<taskId>?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
235|
236|# Task queue
237|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/queue?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
238|
239|# Session status (active, streaming, message count, disk session)
240|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/session/status?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
241|```
242|
243|`GET /status/observability` returns `engine` (status, activeTaskId,
244|activeStageId, activeStageName, activeStageType), `build`, `health`, and
245|`observability` (totals: completed/failed/running/waitingHuman/paused/blocked,
246|plus recent completed/failed lists with failure reasons).
247|
248|### 4b. Via WebSocket (live streaming)
249|
250|The frontend subscribes to `GET /ws?projectId=<projectId>` (WebSocket upgrade).
251|Events are JSON `{ type, sessionId, payload, timestamp }`. Key types:
252|`CONNECTED`, `ENGINE_STATE`, `TASK_UPDATED`, `TASK_DELETED`, `NOTIFICATION`,
253|`PROCESS_STDOUT` / `process:stdout`, and agent events (`agent_start`,
254|`tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`,
255|`message_update`, `error`). The UI's **Live Console** (Observability dashboard)
256|renders these with severity tags (`AGENT`, `CI`, `ERROR`, `HUMAN`, `TOOL`).
257|
258|To watch live from a script, connect to the WebSocket endpoint at
259|`{{kbApiBase}}/ws?projectId=<id>` (upgrade `http`→`ws` / `https`→`wss`) and log
260|incoming frames.
261|
262|### 4c. Via the filesystem
263|
264|For a live task, `task.md` is rewritten on every state change, so
265|`tail -f docs/tasks/<taskId>/task.md` shows frontmatter, `# History`, and
266|`# Log Entries` growing in near-real-time (watch the WebSocket for the
267|live stream itself — see §3d). The `status` frontmatter tells you where it
268|is: `running_agent`, `running_ci`, `running_merge`, `advancing`, `in_stage`,
269|`waiting_human`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed` (`interrupted` after an
270|unclean restart; `running_deploy` is a legacy label from before the deploy
271|runtime was removed). Note: with Runner execution, absolute backend-cwd paths
272|in prompts are retargeted to the task worktree — resolve worktree-relative
273|paths against `kb-<taskId>`, not the backend checkout.
274|
275|---
276|
277|## 5. Analysing a **past** task
278|
279|A "past" task is one that completed, failed, or was parked. Everything you need
280|is on disk — no live service required.
281|
282|1. **Find the task folder.** List task dirs, newest first:
283|
284|   ```bash
285|   ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/
286|   ```
287|
288|   Or find by title/status:
289|
290|   ```bash
291|   grep -rl "status: \"failed\"" {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/*/task.md
292|   ```
293|
294|2. **Read `task.md`** — frontmatter gives status, current stage, timestamps;
295|   `# History` gives the full event timeline; `# Timeline` gives per-stage
296|   durations; `# Log Entries` gives the stored output.
297|
298|3. **Read the stage reports** in the same folder — one per stage run that
299|   produced one (opt-in agent stages + all failure reports), in
300|   filename-timestamp order. They tell you what each stage produced and
301|   whether it passed or failed. Failure reports use the `-failure-` infix.
302|   For stages that did NOT opt in, reconstruct from `# Log Entries`, the
303|   session transcript (worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/`
304|   for embedded runs), and the git history.
305|
306|4. **Reconstruct the failure.** For a failed task, check:
307|   - `status: "failed"` in frontmatter.
308|   - The last `# History` entries (e.g. `Stage failed: <reason>`).
309|   - The FAILED stage report (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`; contains
310|     the error and fallback routing).
311|   - `# Log Entries` tail for the actual error output.
312|   - The API's observability `recentFailed` list (if the service is up) for
313|     `failureReason` / `lastError`.
314|
315|5. **Cross-check the deploy** (if the task reached a deploy command — deploys
316|   run as ordinary CI stages now): see `<deploy-state-dir>/history.jsonl`
317|   and `last-result.json` for whether the deploy succeeded and which build
318|   went live.
319|
320|---
321|
322|## 6. Common analysis recipes
323|
324|### "Why did this task fail?"
325|
326|```bash
327|TASK={{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>
328|grep -E "status|currentStageId" "$TASK/task.md"          # where it ended
329|grep -E "^- " "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20                 # last history events
330|grep -rl "FAILED" "$TASK"/*-failure-*.md                  # failed stage reports
331|grep -E "Log Entries" -A 5 "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20    # stored log tail
332|```
333|
334|### "What is running right now?"
335|
336|```bash
337|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
338|```
339|
340|### "Did the last deploy work / what build is live?"
341|
342|```bash
343|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
344|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
345|tail -n 50 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
346|```
347|
348|### "What did the agent actually do in stage X?"
349|
350|Read any stage report `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md` or
351|`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md` (summary, output, modified files) plus
352|the `# Log Entries` section of `task.md`. Agent stages that did not opt into
353|reporting leave no success report — use the session transcript (Runner
354|worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs) and
355|git log.
356|
357|### "Is the service healthy?"
358|
359|```bash
360|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
361|docker compose logs --tail 50 backend          # Docker deployment
362|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 50   # native self-host
363|```
364|
365|---
366|
367|## 7. Gotchas
368|
369|- **Task data is under the project `cwd`, not `{{deployDir}}`.** The deployed
370|  build dir only holds code + `build.json`.
371|- **`task.md` is a snapshot, not a full transcript.** Stored logs are capped
372|  (`KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT`, default 500 entries, oldest evicted under
373|  a marker). For the full agent conversation use the session transcript —
374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

7|# KainBain Task Analysis (production)
8|
9|This skill teaches an agent how to investigate **live** and **past** KainBain
10|tasks in a production deployment. It covers the two things you almost always
11|need first: **where the task folder is** and **where the logs are**. Everything
12|else is reading those artifacts.
13|
14|KainBain is an AI task orchestrator. Tasks are created into a project's
15|workflow, advance through stages (`agent`, `human`, `ci`, `merge`), and are
16|persisted as markdown on disk. (Legacy `review` stages read as `human`, and
17|legacy `script` / `deploy` stages read as `ci` — a deploy command is an
18|ordinary CI stage now.) Agent stages run on **Runners**: the backend curates
19|the stage prompt and a Runner executes it in a per-task worktree, syncing
20|task docs/assets in and rewriting the backend cwd prefix to the worktree.
21|The API is Fastify; the frontend is served from the same origin. Production
22|is either Docker Compose (`docker compose up -d`, `https://<app-host>`) or a
23|native self-host where the app runs as a systemd **user** service.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. Example deployment profiles (illustrative, optional)
28|
29|| | Dev | Production |
30|| --- | --- | --- |
31|| Repo / project cwd | `{{projectCwd}}` | same repo, but the *deployed* copy is `{{deployDir}}` |
32|| API base | `{{kbApiBase}}` (or `PORT` env) | the public URL / service `PORT` (override `{{kbApiBase}}` — localhost is dev-only) |
33|| Service | none (run manually) | Docker Compose service, or `<service-unit>` (systemd **user** unit on native self-hosts) |
34|| App URL | `{{kbApiBase}}` | `https://<app-host>` |
35|| Task folders | `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/` | same layout, under the project's `cwd` |
36|| Agent execution | embedded (in-process) | Runner worktree (`kb-<taskId>`, cwd prefix retargeted) |
37|
38|**Key fact:** task folders are written under the **project's `cwd`**, not under
39|`{{deployDir}}`. The project's `cwd` is recorded in
40|`<project cwd>/.kainbain/project.json` (e.g. `"cwd": "{{projectCwd}}"`).
41|Tasks live at:
42|
43|```text
44|{{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>/
45|```
46|
47|`{{deployDir}}` is only the *deployed build* (api + frontend/dist + build.json);
48|it does **not** hold task data. Don't look for tasks there.
49|
50|---
51|
52|## 2. The task folder (the single most important artifact)
53|
54|Every task is a directory under `<project cwd>/docs/tasks/<taskId>/`:
55|
56|```text
57|docs/tasks/<taskId>/
58|├── task.md                      # canonical task entity (frontmatter + body)
59|├── IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md       # plan written by the Plan stage (if used)
60|├── plan-<timestamp>.md          # stage report: Plan (only if the stage opted in)
61|├── <stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md  # failure report (ALWAYS written on stage failure)
62|├── automated-tests-<timestamp>.md # CI / human-checkpoint report (always written)
63|└── ...                          # one report per stage run that produced one
64|```
65|
66|**Reporting is opt-in for agent stages.** A default agent stage writes NO
67|report on success — no agent-authored summary file and no engine-generated
68|one. A stage opts in via `report: true` on the stage config or by attaching
69|the `stage-report` skill. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
70|are always written on stage failure, and CI stages (including legacy
71|`script` / `deploy` commands) and merge stages and human checkpoints always
72|write their own reports.
73|
74|### `task.md` — the canonical record
75|
76|`task.md` is the authoritative, server-written snapshot of the task. Read it
77|first. It has YAML frontmatter and a markdown body:
78|
79|- **Frontmatter:** `id`, `projectId`, `workflowId`, `title`, `status`,
80|  `currentStageId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `enteredStageAt`, `timeInStage`,
81|  `outputReport`, `feedback`, `blockedBy` (plus machine fields such as
82|  `branch`, `reportMetadata`, `timelineMetadata`).
83|- **`# Goal`** — the task's goal/title.
84|- **`# History`** — an append-only audit trail, one line per event:
85|  `- <ISO timestamp>: <action>` (created, edited, stage advanced, failed, etc.).
86|  This is the fastest way to reconstruct what happened and when.
87|- **`# Timeline`** — one line per stage visit (`<timestamp>: <stage> |
88|  <status> | <duration>`, with a diff stat when the stage touched git).
89|- **`# Log Entries`** — the stored per-task log as structured JSON, capped at
90|  `KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT` entries (default 500, oldest evicted under
91|  a marker). This is the single bound on task log storage. (Very old files may
92|  still carry a rendered `# Process Logs` section instead — legacy files are
93|  parsed back into entries on load.)
94|- `KAINBAIN_PROCESS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` (default 32000) only bounds one stage's
95|  captured streamed output kept in memory **while it runs** — it is not the
96|  stored task log.
97|
98|### Stage report files (`<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`, `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
99|
100|Agent-stage success reports are **opt-in** (stage `report: true` or the
101|`stage-report` skill). Failure reports always exist and carry the `-failure-`
102|filename infix. Auto-generated reports carry the marker
103|`<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->` (hidden in most renderers).
104|A report contains: task, stage type, model, duration, status (PASSED/FAILED),
105|summary of changes, execution output, modified files, and verification status.
106|On failure it includes the error and notes the fallback routing.
107|
108|### `docs/tasks/active/`
109|
110|A separate, manually-maintained scratch area (`docs/tasks/active/<taskId>/N.md`)
111|holds working notes per stage. It is **not** written by the API — treat it as
112|human scratch, not authoritative.
113|

202|
203|The stored agent/tool/CI output for a task is the `# Log Entries` section of
204|`task.md` (see §2). Live output streams over the WebSocket as `PROCESS_STDOUT`
205|/ `process:stdout` frames, which is what the UI's Live Console renders — for a
206|running task, watch the socket (see §4b), not the file. `task.md` is
207|rewritten on every state change, so its frontmatter, `# History`, and
208|`# Log Entries` stay current, but there is no rendered process-log tail to
209|`tail -f` anymore.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 4. Analysing a **live** task
214|
215|A "live" task is one currently executing or queued. The engine is a single
216|global executor (`ExecutionQueue`) with an `engineState` snapshot.
217|
218|### 4a. Via the API (fastest, no filesystem)
219|
220|```bash
221|# Engine state: what is running right now
222|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
223|
224|# Full observability: engine + health + build + task metrics
225|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
226|
227|# Health
228|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
229|
230|# List tasks for a project (projectId optional → active project)
231|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
232|
233|# Single task (full state incl. history, reports, log entries)
234|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/<taskId>?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
235|
236|# Task queue
237|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/tasks/queue?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
238|
239|# Session status (active, streaming, message count, disk session)
240|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/session/status?projectId=<projectId>" | jq
241|```
242|
243|`GET /status/observability` returns `engine` (status, activeTaskId,
244|activeStageId, activeStageName, activeStageType), `build`, `health`, and
245|`observability` (totals: completed/failed/running/waitingHuman/paused/blocked,
246|plus recent completed/failed lists with failure reasons).
247|
248|### 4b. Via WebSocket (live streaming)
249|
250|The frontend subscribes to `GET /ws?projectId=<projectId>` (WebSocket upgrade).
251|Events are JSON `{ type, sessionId, payload, timestamp }`. Key types:
252|`CONNECTED`, `ENGINE_STATE`, `TASK_UPDATED`, `TASK_DELETED`, `NOTIFICATION`,
253|`PROCESS_STDOUT` / `process:stdout`, and agent events (`agent_start`,
254|`tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_update`, `tool_execution_end`,
255|`message_update`, `error`). The UI's **Live Console** (Observability dashboard)
256|renders these with severity tags (`AGENT`, `CI`, `ERROR`, `HUMAN`, `TOOL`).
257|
258|To watch live from a script, connect to the WebSocket endpoint at
259|`{{kbApiBase}}/ws?projectId=<id>` (upgrade `http`→`ws` / `https`→`wss`) and log
260|incoming frames.
261|
262|### 4c. Via the filesystem
263|
264|For a live task, `task.md` is rewritten on every state change, so
265|`tail -f docs/tasks/<taskId>/task.md` shows frontmatter, `# History`, and
266|`# Log Entries` growing in near-real-time (watch the WebSocket for the
267|live stream itself — see §3d). The `status` frontmatter tells you where it
268|is: `running_agent`, `running_ci`, `running_merge`, `advancing`, `in_stage`,
269|`waiting_human`, `paused`, `failed`, `completed` (`interrupted` after an
270|unclean restart; `running_deploy` is a legacy label from before the deploy
271|runtime was removed). Note: with Runner execution, absolute backend-cwd paths
272|in prompts are retargeted to the task worktree — resolve worktree-relative
273|paths against `kb-<taskId>`, not the backend checkout.
274|
275|---
276|
277|## 5. Analysing a **past** task
278|
279|A "past" task is one that completed, failed, or was parked. Everything you need
280|is on disk — no live service required.
281|
282|1. **Find the task folder.** List task dirs, newest first:
283|
284|   ```bash
285|   ls -lt {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/
286|   ```
287|
288|   Or find by title/status:
289|
290|   ```bash
291|   grep -rl "status: \"failed\"" {{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/*/task.md
292|   ```
293|
294|2. **Read `task.md`** — frontmatter gives status, current stage, timestamps;
295|   `# History` gives the full event timeline; `# Timeline` gives per-stage
296|   durations; `# Log Entries` gives the stored output.
297|
298|3. **Read the stage reports** in the same folder — one per stage run that
299|   produced one (opt-in agent stages + all failure reports), in
300|   filename-timestamp order. They tell you what each stage produced and
301|   whether it passed or failed. Failure reports use the `-failure-` infix.
302|   For stages that did NOT opt in, reconstruct from `# Log Entries`, the
303|   session transcript (worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/`
304|   for embedded runs), and the git history.
305|
306|4. **Reconstruct the failure.** For a failed task, check:
307|   - `status: "failed"` in frontmatter.
308|   - The last `# History` entries (e.g. `Stage failed: <reason>`).
309|   - The FAILED stage report (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`; contains
310|     the error and fallback routing).
311|   - `# Log Entries` tail for the actual error output.
312|   - The API's observability `recentFailed` list (if the service is up) for
313|     `failureReason` / `lastError`.
314|
315|5. **Cross-check the deploy** (if the task reached a deploy command — deploys
316|   run as ordinary CI stages now): see `<deploy-state-dir>/history.jsonl`
317|   and `last-result.json` for whether the deploy succeeded and which build
318|   went live.
319|
320|---
321|
322|## 6. Common analysis recipes
323|
324|### "Why did this task fail?"
325|
326|```bash
327|TASK={{projectCwd}}/docs/tasks/<taskId>
328|grep -E "status|currentStageId" "$TASK/task.md"          # where it ended
329|grep -E "^- " "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20                 # last history events
330|grep -rl "FAILED" "$TASK"/*-failure-*.md                  # failed stage reports
331|grep -E "Log Entries" -A 5 "$TASK/task.md" | tail -20    # stored log tail
332|```
333|
334|### "What is running right now?"
335|
336|```bash
337|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/observability" | jq '.engine'
338|```
339|
340|### "Did the last deploy work / what build is live?"
341|
342|```bash
343|cat {{deployDir}}/build.json
344|cat <deploy-state-dir>/last-result.json
345|tail -n 50 <deploy-state-dir>/deploy.log
346|```
347|
348|### "What did the agent actually do in stage X?"
349|
350|Read any stage report `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md` or
351|`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md` (summary, output, modified files) plus
352|the `# Log Entries` section of `task.md`. Agent stages that did not opt into
353|reporting leave no success report — use the session transcript (Runner
354|worktree on the Runner host, or `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs) and
355|git log.
356|
357|### "Is the service healthy?"
358|
359|```bash
360|curl -s "{{kbApiBase}}/status/health" | jq
361|docker compose logs --tail 50 backend          # Docker deployment
362|journalctl --user -u <service-unit> -p err -n 50   # native self-host
363|```
364|
365|---
366|
367|## 7. Gotchas
368|
369|- **Task data is under the project `cwd`, not `{{deployDir}}`.** The deployed
370|  build dir only holds code + `build.json`.
371|- **`task.md` is a snapshot, not a full transcript.** Stored logs are capped
372|  (`KAINBAIN_LOG_ENTRIES_MAX_COUNT`, default 500 entries, oldest evicted under
373|  a marker). For the full agent conversation use the session transcript —
374|  Runner worktree on the Runner host, or the session JSONL in
375|  `.kainbain/sessions/` for embedded runs.
376|- **`.kainbain/` is gitignored** — session transcripts and deploy state are
377|  local-only, not in the repo. Runner worktrees (`kb-<taskId>`) are also
378|  local to the Runner host.
379|- **Absolute backend paths are retargeted on Runners.** The backend curates
380|  prompts with its own project cwd and the Runner rewrites that prefix to
381|  the prepared worktree — a path that exists on the backend may live under
382|  the worktree on the Runner host.
383|- **There is no `deploy` stage type anymore.** Legacy `deploy` (like `script`)
384|  reads as `ci`; merge-plus-deploy composites are migrated into a git-only
385|  merge stage plus a dedicated CI stage. `running_deploy` in old records is a
386|  legacy label.
387|- **`docs/tasks/active/` is human scratch**, not API-written. Don't treat it as
388|  authoritative.
389|- **Auto-generated reports** are marked with
390|  `<!-- KAINBAIN AUTO-GENERATED REPORT -->`; distinguish them from manual ones.
391|- **Agent-stage success reports are opt-in.** A default agent stage that
392|  succeeded leaves NO report file — absence of a `<stage-slug>-<timestamp>.md`
393|  is expected, not data loss. Failure reports (`<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`)
394|  are always written.
395|- **The engine is single-threaded** (one global `ExecutionQueue`). Only one
396|  task executes at a time; others queue. `engine.status` is `idle` when nothing
397|  runs.
398|- **Interrupted tasks** (server restart mid-run) are rehydrated with status
399|  `interrupted` and a history entry "Execution recovered after server restart".
400|- **Auto-iteration:** a failed stage may auto re-run (fix → re-test → re-review)
401|  up to `KAINBAIN_MAX_AUTO_ITERATIONS` (default 8) before being parked as
402|  `failed`. Each failed attempt leaves a `<stage-slug>-failure-<timestamp>.md`
403|  report; multiple failure files for the same stage = auto-iteration attempts.

Read text file `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`.
1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.

Read text file `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`.
1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
105|  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
106|  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
107|  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
108|  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
109|  wrapper, above).
110|- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
111|  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
112|  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
113|  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.
114|
115|## Per-runner version setting
116|
117|Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
118|the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:
119|
120|- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
121|  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
122|  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
123|  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
124|  wait for idle) to converge it.
125|- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
126|  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
127|  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
128|  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
129|  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
130|  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
131|  move forward.
132|
133|The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
134|first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
135|minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.
136|
137|## Triage: a runner says out of date
138|
139|Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
140|doctor is read-only and never writes:
141|
142|```
143|$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
144|```
145|
146|Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:
147|
148|- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
149|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
150|  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
151|  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
152|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
153|  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
154|  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
155|  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
156|  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
157|  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
158|  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
159|  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
160|  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
161|  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
162|- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
166|  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
167|  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
168|  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
169|  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
170|  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
171|  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
172|  update them manually.
173|- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
174|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
175|  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
176|  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
177|  reason like an "update failed" below.
178|- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
179|  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
180|  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
181|  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
182|  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
183|  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
184|  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
185|  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
186|  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
187|  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
188|  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
189|  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
190|  and the next idle check retries.
191|- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
192|  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
193|  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
194|  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.
195|
196|Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
197|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
198|for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
199|`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
200|was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).

# RESPONSE — follow-up solutions for "high level of interruptions"

Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: triage of `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` + replication guides into
reviewable, parallelisable follow-up tasks.

Inputs reviewed: `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (6 causes + amplifier, 118 interrupts surveyed
across 61 tasks in project `0fd41821`), `REPLICATION-INDEX.md`, `GUIDE-01`–`GUIDE-07`,
`TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`, and `assets/image.png` (task `7f6220c3` timeline showing repeated
"Auto-resumed after server restart" rows and inflated "Tried N times" badges).
Key code seams were spot-checked in the repo (`executionLedger.js`,
`autoResumeTask.js`, `daemon.js` cap branch, `project.js` cap refusal) and match the
analysis. No prod commands were run; all prod procedures below are quoted from the
guides as procedures for a later permitted step.

## Triage verdict: what is worth tackling

| Cause (per WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS) | Evidence strength | Tackle? | Solution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Worktree-cap exhaustion loop (49/118, reason-proven) | high | **Yes** | S1: stop counting cap refusals as deaths + add re-dispatch backoff |
| 2. HTTP 413 on `complete-execution` (5 proven, ≤15 suspected) | high (proven case) | **Yes** | S2: raise/shrink the completion payload + never crash-loop on 413 |
| 3. local-alpha setup-phase deaths (~60 bare/fast, fault unnamed) | medium (localised, root unknown) | **Yes, investigate first** | S3: prod-journal investigation (E1/E6), then a targeted fix from findings |

## S4 — Make in-assignment transient backend errors non-fatal (daemon containment)

**Answers Cause 4 (501 `fetch failed` + 16 `Backend 502` since 11-19 on server2-alpha;
a proven 502 window 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 during backend build 637).** Today any
in-`try` backend-call failure inside `executeAssignment` sends an interrupt and
rethrows → process exit → systemd restart. Heartbeat failures are tolerated (lease
TTL) but in-assignment call failures are fatal, so every LAN blip or backend restart
window can kill a run.

**Proposed change (runner, `runner/daemon.js` + `runner/client.js`):**
1. In the `executeAssignment` catch (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2452`): transient backend
   errors (`fetch failed` network errors, 502/503/504 status) during an assignment
   send an interrupt *with reason* and **return** (keep polling) instead of rethrowing —
   the same report-and-return precedent as the existing `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` and
   deterministic-`gitFailure` branches. Lease TTL already bounds the damage.

   so the idle loop stops crash-cycling (restart counters 366→367 in the 11-19 sample)

   genuinely unknown errors — enumerate the non-fatal set explicitly (status codes +
   `fetch failed` cause) rather than inverting the catch-all, so new failure modes

## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)

Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):

1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
   an authenticated runner daemon.

Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).

|---|---|---|

| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |

Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.

Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle

## 3. Possible causes

### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)

**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
suspected death loop.

**Pros (for).**
- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
  (`/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` =
  server2-alpha host).
- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

**Cons (against).**
- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
  both hosts).
- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
  (48 bare) needs a different driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
  same-runner re-claim.
- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).

### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)

**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

**Pros (for).**
- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
  11-20 (18).
- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
  (only uncaught fallible step there).
- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.

**Cons (against).**
- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
  restart counters are unknown from here.
- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`

  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.

- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.
- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).
- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post

# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — high level of task interruptions

Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: DO research (investigatory only — no solutions proposed).

## 0. Inputs

- **Bug report**: many tasks end with interruptions suggesting flakiness; reporter
  notes a `local-alpha` runner restart-loop incident and wonders if it is related;
  interruptions "should happen rarely but they are seemingly quite common".
- **Screenshot** (`assets/image.png`): task `7f6220c3` ("add support for projects
  having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo") showing repeated
  "Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and high
  "Tried N times" counts (Merge resolver ×6, Quick review ×6, Automated
  tests ×10, In Progress ×11).
- **Survey result**: the Questionnaire stage recorded `Survey completed (none)` —
  the `question-me` skill requested no survey questions, so there is no
  `SURVEY.md` with human answers. All evidence below comes from repo code,
  the live backend API, runner worktrees, and the runner systemd journal.

## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)

Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):

1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):
   the runner drops its lease and the task re-queues as `interrupted`, history
   `Runner <id> interrupted execution <exec> — lease dropped, re-queues as
   interrupted[ — Reason: <reason>]`. This is the ONLY writer of that history
   string, and the route requires runner auth, so every such entry was sent by
   an authenticated runner daemon.

Recovery: `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) flips
`interrupted` → `in_stage` with Rule-0 queue priority and history
`Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` — **including when no
server restart happened** (runner-path interrupts resume through the same
function via `scheduleTick`, pickup ≈150ms per `performStartupRecovery` docs in
`api/flow/startupRecovery.js`). Anti-loop guard: consecutive interrupts on the
same task+stage increment `runnerInterruptCount`; at `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`
(`api/flow/executionLedger.js:17`) the task is parked for the operator
(`runner-death-loop` in `api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`).

## 2. Fleet-wide numbers (live backend, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21)

| Signal | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Runner-path interrupts (`interrupted execution`) | 118 | across 30/61 tasks (~half the project) |
| Server-restart interrupts (`interrupted by server restart`) | **0** | no task, ever in retained history |
| `Execution recovered after server restart` | **0** | same |
| `Auto-resumed after server restart` entries | 100 | label fires for runner interrupts too |
| Runner split | local-alpha 96 / server2-alpha 22 | local-alpha dominates 4:1 |
| With `Reason:` suffix | 49 | **all 49 are the same reason** (Cause 1) |
| Bare (no reason) | 69 | cause invisible from backend history |
| Interrupt ≤15s after `started` (median 4.7s) | 99 | dies before/without `prompted`, i.e. in worktree setup |
| Interrupt ≥2min after `started` | 15 | post-harness: commit/push/complete phase |
| Death-streak escalations (`Runner deaths escalated`) | 42 | tasks parked at count ≥ 5 |

Timing detail: between the runner's `started` and `prompted` progress events
(`runner/daemon.js:1975` → `:2061`) the only uncaught fallible step is
`prepareWorkdir` (`runner/daemon.js:1984`; doc-sync and prompt-report are
try/caught). So a `started` → interrupt gap of seconds with no `prompted` event
localises the fault to worktree preparation (or the process dying there).
Between `finished` (`runner/daemon.js:2213`) and completion sit `commitAndPush`,
`sendLogs`, verdict, `collectTaskFiles`, and `client.complete`.

Deployed runner vintage: live runners report `0.1.0`, built from main
`f430f53` (2026-11-11); repo is at `0.2.0`. The deployed build HAS the 10-29
worktree-cap graceful path (`25feee39`) but LACKS the 11-21 interrupt-reason
and deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in
`7ac148ce`). Runner rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle
converge (`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so rollout lag is expected.

## 3. Possible causes

### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)

**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
suspected death loop.

**Pros (for).**
- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
  (`/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` =
  server2-alpha host).
- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

**Cons (against).**
- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
  both hosts).
- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
  (48 bare) needs a different driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
  same-runner re-claim.
- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).

### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)

**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
(`api

backend restart/502 window.

## 4. Amplifier (not a root cause): re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake

These do not initiate interrupts, but they turn each one into the screenshot's
"quite common" impression and into parked tasks:

- **Instant priority re-dispatch, no backoff.** Every interrupt flips to
  `in_stage` with Rule-0 priority and dispatches in ~150ms
  (`performStartupRecovery`, `scheduleTick.js:178-181`, `findResumedCandidate`),
  so the same failing runner re-claims immediately — tight loops (18s laps on
  `c5c465c4`) instead of spaced retries, and no window for the sibling runner
  or the operator to intervene.
- **Death counter counts capacity refusals as deaths.** `interruptExecution`
  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — including graceful
  `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` refusals where nothing died. Five cap refusals on one
  stage = `runner-death-loop` park (`isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57`),
  mislabelling a full disk-table as dying runners (42 escalations fleet-wide;
  `c5c465c4` hit 27).
- **`Tried N times` counts resumes as tries.** `summarizeStageRuns`
  (`frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`) sets `tryCount`
  to the number of grouped timeline rows per stage — `Advanced` + `Moved` +
  `Failed` + every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one, `autoResumeTask`
  `:71-78`). Genuine failback cycles (e.g. four `CI command failed with exit
  code 1` round-trips on `7f6220c3`) and interrupt/resume cycles are summed
  into one scary number.
- **`Auto-resumed after server restart` mislabels runner interrupts.**
  `autoResumeTask` uses one history string for both recovery routes, so 100
  runner-path resumes display as server restarts that never happened (0
  recorded) — directly feeding the "server flake" reading of the report.

### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)

**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
suspected death loop.

**Pros (for).**
- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)

  server2-alpha host).
- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

**Cons (against).**
- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
  both hosts).
- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike

### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)

**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

**Pros (for).**
- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
  11-20 (18).
- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
  (only uncaught fallible step there).
- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.

**Cons (against).**
- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
  restart counters are unknown from here.
- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.
- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).
- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
  `finished`).

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix

- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
